# Synthetic verified requirement record
Fictional inputs, supplied as checked and current for this draft.
E1: Approved interface baseline supports exact ticket-ID lookup and returns either one matching ticket or not-found.
E2: Approved business rule allows exact lookup of closed tickets within the already-approved 180-day retention period.
E3: Current acceptance script passes exact lookup for ticket T-017, not-found for T-999, and lookup of closed T-018 within 180 days.
Scope is a two-requirement draft; production deployment and broader policy changes are not authorized.

files.inputs/requirement-gap-record.md:
# Synthetic requirement evidence with a material gap
All records are fictional.
E1: Current approved interface supports exact ticket-ID lookup and a not-found response.
E2: Approved service policy rev 3 requires closed-ticket availability for 180 days.
E3: Signed customer agreement rev 2 requires the same closed tickets to remain available for 365 days.
The applicability and precedence of E2 and E3 are unresolved, and no responsible-owner decision exists. The user authorizes a draft and evidence analysis, not a retention-policy change.

files.inputs/ticket-api-boundary.md:
# Synthetic ticket API boundaries
This is a fictional design exercise.
Browser clients send ticket IDs over the network. Service tickets carry tenant_id and customer contact information. An existing identity provider authenticates users and provides verified user and tenant claims. The database is private to the service. Production rollout and real account changes are out of scope. Required behavior is that a user can retrieve only tickets from their own organization, including safe not-found/denied handling without exposing another organization's ticket metadata.
